page: Amazon Web Services r8gn.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized virtual machine based on AWS Graviton4 silicon. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a single dedicated physical core (1 vCPU) using the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 microarchitecture clocked at 2.8 GHz. It features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by 8.0 GB of system memory, matching the standard 1:8 core-to-memory ratio of the R-family.

Hardware capabilities omit local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached EBS storage and standard network interfaces offering a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps. Hardware-accelerated AES cryptography instructions are present, while x86-specific instruction sets and AVX extensions are absent.

Benchmark results demonstrate adequate single-threaded efficiency against severe multi-threaded and absolute throughput constraints. In Geekbench tests, single-core processing achieved 1748.0, and stress-ng reached 1694.69, positioning single-core execution within median ranges. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered strong throughput at 14.26 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics mirror single-thread figures due to the single-core topology, leading to low ratings in aggregate compute, Redis throughput (2.29 million operations/sec), and PassMark CPU metrics.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, r8gn.medium offers an economical footprint for applications that demand high memory density per core without requiring high parallel processing. It is best suited for small in-memory caches, development environments, lightweight background workers, and low-traffic database instances.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gn.medium is an entry-level memory-optimized instance featuring 1 vCPU and 1 dedicated physical core based on the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture at 2.8 GHz. Paired with 8.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The Nitro-managed VM provides a baseline network speed of 3 Gbps, contains no local storage, and includes no GPUs. In performance benchmarks, single-threaded metrics such as single-core Geekbench (1748.0) and bzip3 decompression (14.26 GB/sec) show competitive execution efficiency, though overall throughput is constrained by the single-core footprint. PassMark CPU scores and aggregate parallel throughput rank in the lowest percentiles. Due to its memory density and dedicated core architecture, r8gn.medium provides a cost-effective, low-overhead deployment target for lightweight in-memory caching, low-volume database engines, development workloads, and single-threaded worker tasks.
